subject: Biology
title: What Is a Mutation?
description: A quick win: understand What Is a Mutation?.

hook.text: A mutation is any change in the DNA sequence. It can be as small as swapping one single letter.

buildup.text: Mutations happen during DNA copying, from radiation, chemicals, or just random chance.

discovery.text: Most mutations are harmless or silent—they don't change the protein at all.

twist.text: Rarely, a mutation creates something useful. Blue eyes arose from a single mutation about 10,000 years ago.

climax.text: Mutations are the raw material of evolution—without them, life could never adapt.

punchline.text: Typos in DNA drive all of evolution.

details.summary: A mutation is any change to the DNA sequence, from a single base substitution to large chromosomal rearrangements. Mutations can be caused by replication errors, radiation, chemicals, or viruses, and may be beneficial, harmful, or neutral in their effects.
details.whyItMatters: Mutations are both the engine of evolution and the cause of genetic disease. Every inherited trait variation traces back to a mutation event. Understanding mutations is fundamental to genetics, medicine, and evolutionary biology.
takeaways: Mutations range from single-base changes to large chromosomal alterations
DNA repair systems fix most replication errors before they become permanent
Only germline mutations are inherited; somatic mutations affect one individual

faq.question: Are most mutations harmful?
faq.answer: No. Most mutations are neutral because they occur in non-coding DNA or produce silent changes in codons. Of those affecting proteins, many are mildly deleterious. Truly beneficial mutations are rare but are the ones natural selection preserves.

faq.question: What is the difference between germline and somatic mutations?
faq.answer: Germline mutations occur in eggs or sperm and are passed to all cells of the offspring and future generations. Somatic mutations occur in body cells during lifetime and are not inherited. Cancer typically results from accumulated somatic mutations.
